title: Zions Bank CEO Teaches Salt Lake City Students How to Save for a Rainy Day
summary: President and CEO Nate Callister taught second-grade students at Backman Elementary School the importance of saving for a rainy day.
body_markdown:
SALT LAKE CITY, Utah; April 21, 2026 — At a time when economic uncertainty is putting money decisions under the spotlight, Backman Elementary School students are learning how to take charge of their financial futures.


In honor of National Teach Children to Save Day, second grade students at Backman Elementary School received a lesson on the importance of saving for a rainy day from Zions Bank President and CEO Nate Callister. Callister presented each child with a newly minted $2 bill, encouraging the students to double down on their savings goals. Annika Hunt, alpine skiier on the U.S. Ski Team, joined Callister for his lesson.


“Financial literacy is a powerful tool to help students build resilience,” Callister said. “By teaching children the basics of saving for a rainy day, we’re not just preparing them for a financial emergency — we’re giving them the confidence and skills to help navigate all of life’s financial challenges.”


Callister is among the dozens of Zions Bank employees who are volunteering in classrooms across Utah and Idaho in April to teach more than 6,200 children the fundamentals of saving, budgeting, and smart money management. The need for early financial education is particularly important today. According to arecent survey from Bankrate , over half of Americans lack the savings to cover a $1,000 emergency expense. Additionally, nearly one in three Americans have more credit card debt than emergency savings.


Zions Bank’s hands-on lessons aim to equip students with the skills they need to develop healthy financial habits from a young age. The program covers topics such as setting savings goals, understanding needs versus wants, and the power of compound interest.


National Teach Children to Save Day is an initiative of the American Bankers Association designed to promote financial education for young students. Zions Bank has participated in the program for more than 24 years, reinforcing its commitment to financial literacy and community engagement. Since 2002, Zions employees have collectively taught more than 200,000 students as part of Teach Children to Save Day.


**About Zions Bank**

Zions Bank also operates 26 branches in Idaho and Wyoming. In addition to offering a wide range of traditional banking services, Zions Bank is also a leader in small business lending.
